title: Good so far.
body:
Just started using it, but I notice stuff that I am missing. There's a lot to like here but I'm surprised to not find a 'dark mode' for a more pleasant experience. Bit annoying It's only in compatability mode on ipad and when I tried logging in i had to spend 5 minutes clicking prompts and questions to login and being bombarded with emails for the same mail i used on account, I was then logged out of my phone. 

 No ability to set specific goals on select days in the week. A bit overwhelming and cluttered at times. This is my first impression though. Lovely vivid art and gamified design and decent content. I can see this will help with routines. However for an app that's been around this long and at this price point I'd expect a more streamlined experience, more options, languages, dark mode, more customizable settings and options, hopefully it is still being tweaked and improved. Will update this review as time progresses if I stick around.

PS. A bit shady tactic when selecting 30 day trial and "15 minutes to decide", I couldn't see what the price was or what the subscription was until after I paid 1 dollar with PayPal, then had to find my way through the app to subscription field to see it was annually. This is something that could be more easily clarified to the customers. This should be completely unnecessary and causes mistrust and bad reviews. This tactic is used in shady ads and Facebook schemes to manipulate user psychology and FOMO. Not a good first impression.

author: Elin Magn

title: Effective but busy
body:
I’m loving the core principles of this app and the interactions to build up habits and routines. The downside for me has been how cluttered and chaotic it feels at times. I just want to be eased into adopting new routines. It feels at times like the number of pings, letters, messages and prompts to do various things or try this/that feature detracts from the core goal of building a routine.

Circles and Discover seem superfluous for a beginner. I understand that the social element is important, but again it feels like clutter as an early-stage user. Personally, I don’t find it useful to have a distinct “social” area in the app. To be honest I’ve all but ignored those two areas of the app so far, about 10 days in.

Could do with toning down the push prompts. This isn’t the only app I use daily for my mental health and it seems counter-productive to bury myself in notifications when the goal is a more mindful, effective day.

Aside from that, a bug I’m seeing: the “Journey” tab is empty (or at least is entirely white space).
